title: Event Emitter Dispatch Log
prompt: Replay a list of operations against an in-memory event emitter and return the dispatch log. Operations are `{ op: "on" | "once", event, id, emits? }`, `{ op: "off", event, id }`, and `{ op: "emit", event, payload }`. Listeners on `"*"` receive every event, after that event's own listeners. Each call logs `"<id>:<event>:<payload>"`. A listener with `emits: { event, payload }` dispatches that event immediately when it runs (depth-first, before the next listener of the outer event). Rules: take a snapshot of the listeners when a dispatch starts; a `once` listener is detached right before it runs and never runs twice, even if it is still in an outer snapshot; subscribing the same `id` to the same event twice is a no-op; `off` for an unknown id does nothing; a dispatch with no listeners logs `"unhandled:<event>"`; a top-level emit is depth 1 and a dispatch deeper than 10 logs `"overflow:<event>"` instead of running.

explanation.beginner: Keep a Map from event name to a list of listeners, in the order they subscribed. `on` and `once` add to the list (unless that id is already there), and `off` removes the first listener with that id. Emitting is a small recursive function: copy the event's list, add the `*` list after it, and walk the copy. For each listener write the log line; if it has `emits`, call the same emit function right away for that event with depth + 1, then carry on with the next listener. The copy matters: if a listener changes the subscriptions, the dispatch you are in keeps going with the list it started with. A `once` listener gets a `fired` flag: set it and remove the listener before running it, and skip it if the flag is already set. Finally, check the depth first so a listener that re-emits its own event stops after ten levels instead of looping forever.
explanation.junior: This mirrors real emitter semantics (Node's EventEmitter snapshots listeners per emit and wraps `once` handlers with a fired flag). The two hidden traps are both about re-entrancy. First, detach a `once` listener before invoking it, otherwise its own nested emit calls it again. Second, the outer snapshot still holds a reference to a `once` listener that already fired in a nested dispatch; removing it from the Map is not enough, you need the per-listener `fired` flag. Detach by identity rather than by id, so an unrelated re-subscription with the same id is not removed by accident. Model ops as a discriminated union on `op` so the `emit` branch knows `payload` exists. Cost is O(L) per dispatch for the snapshot copy; the depth guard bounds recursion at 10 frames, which also protects the call stack. Edge cases: wildcard-only events are handled (not unhandled), emitting before any subscription, `off` on an event that never had listeners.
